Description: In the Kitchen, Annie Beaumont and Tony Dauer try to extract clues to the truth from Oswald, who is locked in the pantry. Oswald points out that the Chapel may be the only place with answers. Afterwards, the three leave one after another due to an upstairs quarrel and a division of tasks.
Location: Kitchen (Kitchen)
Key Information:
  - After Edmund Galley leaves, Annie Beaumont confirms Oswald is still locked in the pantry and asks about his physical condition.
  - Oswald says Edmund Galley’s gun was not aimed at him and, with a vengeful tone, claims "the owner of the house will get what he deserves."
  - Tony Dauer and Annie Beaumont discuss the gunshot and the non-physical nature of the current events; Oswald agrees the events clearly cannot be explained by normal means.
  - Tony Dauer tries to connect the pocket watch and the word "Rupert" as a key clue, but Annie Beaumont thinks the watch is "too new" and doesn’t fit the characteristics of an ancient historical relic.
  - Oswald says he has never heard of any history related to the watch and points out this doesn’t look like typical "supernatural activity."
  - Annie Beaumont accuses Tony Dauer of having thrown away a doll, which may have triggered the current situation; Tony tries to defend himself.
  - Oswald proposes that the only place that might have answers is the Chapel (Chapel), but the key is on him and he is locked in the pantry, so they cannot go.
  - Tony Dauer asks whether they can force the Chapel door; Oswald warns, "You can try... if you’re not afraid of dying."
  - The three hear loud arguing upstairs; Annie Beaumont decides to go upstairs to check what’s happening.
  - Annie Beaumont tells Tony Dauer to go to her room to fetch "something that can be used to persuade Edmund Galley," and instructs Tony to wait for her in the Attic (Attic).
  - Annie Beaumont then leaves the Kitchen; Tony Dauer also leaves shortly after; Oswald remains in the pantry.
Characters:
  [Annie Beaumont (Annie Beaumont)] Person No. 2.
    · Confirms in the Kitchen that Oswald is locked in the pantry and tries to obtain his explanation of the events.
    · Believes the pocket watch is too new and may not be a traditional supernatural key object.
    · Emotionally accuses Tony Dauer of having thrown away a doll, possibly causing the situation to spiral.
    · After hearing upstairs arguing, decides to go upstairs and assigns Tony Dauer to fetch an item from her room to "persuade Edmund Galley."
    · Tells Tony Dauer to wait for her in the Attic, then leaves the Kitchen first.
  [Oswald (Oswald)] Person No. 3, detained in the pantry.
    · Says Edmund Galley did not aim the gun at him and claims the house’s owner will face retribution.
    · Agrees the current events cannot be explained by physical means and says he has never seen anything like this either.
    · Says the Chapel (Chapel) is the only place that might have answers.
    · Explains that the Chapel key is on him, but since he is imprisoned he cannot take anyone there.
    · Warns that forcing entry into the Chapel could be deadly.
  [Tony Dauer (Tony Dauer)] Person No. 4, Helen Dauer’s son.
    · Discusses the gunshot and possible supernatural explanations with Annie Beaumont, and suggests the pocket watch and the word "Rupert" may be connected.
    · After being accused of throwing away a doll, tries to explain but fails to calm the conflict.
    · As instructed, prepares to go to Annie Beaumont’s room to fetch something, and then heads to the Attic to wait to rendezvous.
